title: Duel Decks: Mind vs. Might: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: To look into its light is to meet the gaze of history.
A skilled Izzet chronarch can carry out an epic vendetta between the fall of one hourglass grain and the next.
"Know one part of the name, obsession begins. Know two parts, paranoia sets in. Know three parts, madness descends. Know all, and only the kami know what will become of you." —Lady Azami
It doesn't matter if the mind or body cracks first. They both have to go.
"The seas are vast, but the skies are even more so. Why be content with one kingdom when I can rule them both?"
The rumors are horrifying; the truth is worse.
It's never just *one* goblin.
Mages often seek to emulate the powerful relics lost to time and apocalypse.
Immolation is the sincerest form of flattery.
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."
"Some relic hunters have given up exploring and gone to fight the Eldrazi. But I know our work is more important than ever. The secrets we uncover could lead to the world's salvation."
Thaumaturges remain silent around chimeras, lest their words conjure even stranger beasts.
It loathes all tastes but two: spells and flesh.
"A massacre? It is a mercy we grant them. This way they won't freeze to death."
The Great Furnace's blessing is a spectacular sight, but the best view comes at a high cost.
"Now everyone knows what you are."
"There's more where that came from!"
Some of the eleven minotaur clans of Mirtiin are expert crafters and learned philosophers. Others just like to hit stuff.
In times when freedom seems lost, great souls arise to reclaim it.
Unhappy with the creation of the wolfir, Rorica broke with her order and led a crusade against the "reformed werewolves."
He does not tolerate intruders.
Treefolk and elves share a common interest in the forests, but really the elves just feel at home with the view from above.
"Clever folk build their homes near cloudcrowns. If a hawk or even just a faerie tries to swoop in, it'll get swatted from here to Cloverdell." —Calydd, kithkin farmer
"Words lie. People lie. The land tells the truth."
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
The safewright Talara protects a delicate woodland waterfall. She has vowed to send wave after wave of warriors to slay any who would dare disturb its beauty.
"Run home, cur. I've already taken your master's head. Don't make me thrash you with it."
"I swore to take one head for each member of my family they killed. My task is nowhere near its end."
Those who regard the Gruul as savage simpletons underestimate the subtle power of their shamans.
A savage cry with the power to shatter minds.
"This city will perish, and the Gruul will cheer as the boar-god crushes the last bricks into dust." —Nikya of the Old Ways
A banner for bonds of blood or belief.
